items.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I remember saying to Jim Davis, I said, “can we have the studio tomorrow?”

ctx.x: Well I have to tell you the story on “West Side Story,” on that album. We had this school, the jazz school in Toronto, called The Advanced School for Contemporary Music, and it

was Ray Brown, Ed Thigpen and myself. And we were teaching there. And I got a call from Verve records and they said, “we would like you to do something on ‘West Side Story.’” And I said, oh, boy, I’d heard some of the score and that’s not easy, you know. So they said, “could you put something together and we’d like to do it soon, because the show is hot, and we’d like to get it out.” You know like record companies, it’s like do it yesterday. So while we were teaching, on off periods, I would call the group…
Oh, yes. Tenderness, fire, and beauty. I know that the composer, Bernstein, I know he loved it. I know he loved it you know. To hear his music interpreted like that.
